'''''Aquilegia dichroa''''' is a [[perennial plant|perennial]] [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Ranunculaceae]], native to Portugal and northwestern Spain.<ref name="POWO"/>

==Description==
''Aquilegia dichroa'' is a perennial [[Herbaceous plant|herb]] growing to {{cvt|18–75|cm|in|0}} tall with an erect stem which is [[Trichome#Aerial surface hairs|pubescent]] towards the top and sticky towards the base. The leaves are green and smooth on the uppersides, and slightly downy underneath. The basal leaves have stalks {{cvt|4–18|cm}} long, the leaves themselves measuring {{cvt|6–7|cm}} long by {{cvt|7–12|cm}} wide. Each has three wedge- or egg-shaped [[Leaflet (botany)|leaflets]], of which the central leaflet always and the side leaflets sometimes have a stalk. The flowers are blue, nodding and have pointed oval [[sepal]]s {{cvt|1.5|cm|in|1}} long, and blue [[petal]]s {{cvt|2|cm|in|1}} long with white tips. The petals have thick, blue, curved [[nectar spur]]s which are hooked at the end and {{cvt|1.2|cm|in|1}} long. The [[stamen]]s are longer than the petals, and the [[anther]]s are yellow, blackening towards the tip.<ref name="Freyn-1880"/>

==Taxonomy==
''Aquilegia dichroa'' was formally described by the Austrian botanist Josef Franz Freyn in 1880. Freyn differentiated the species from the similar ''[[Aquilegia vulgaris]]'' by its small sepals, protruding stamens, hooked [[Style (botany)|styles]], and evenly if not densely hairy leaves.<ref name="Freyn-1880"/> It was reassessed as a subspecies ''dichroa'' of ''A. vulgaris'' by the Spanish botanist Tomás Emilio Díaz in 1984.<ref name="POWO"/>

A closely related species ''A. molleriana'' was described by Freyn and Vinczé von Borbás in 1886<ref name="Borbás-1886"/> but is now considered a synonym of ''A. dichroa''.<ref name="POWO"/>

===Etymology===
The [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''[[wikt:dichroa|dichroa]]'' means "of two colours", referring to the blue-and-white flowers.<ref name="Gledhill-2006"/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Aquilegia dichroa'' is native to Portugal and northwestern Spain, and has been [[Introduced species|introduced]] to the islands of [[Terceira Island|Terceira]], [[Graciosa]], and [[Pico Island|Pico]] in the [[Azores]].<ref name="COL"/> It grows in mountainous areas in granitic soils.<ref name="Borbás-1886"/>

==Conservation==
{{As of|2024|December}}, the species has not been assessed for the [[IUCN Red List]].<ref name="IUCN"/>

==Ecology==
''Aquilegia dichroa'' flowers from April to June.<ref name="Borbás-1886"/> In mainland Portugal it is found in the oak-wood [[plant community]] ''[[Ruscus aculeatus|Rusco aculeati]]-[[Quercus robur|Quercetum roboris]]'' (butcher's-broom and pedunculate oak) along with plants such as ''[[Scilla verna]]'' (spring squill), ''[[Veronica chamaedrys]]'' (germander speedwell), ''[[Hieracium sabaudum]]'' (European hawkweed), and ''[[Melampyrum pratense]]'' (common cow-wheat).<ref name="Raposo-2023"/>
